schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The -2- edge of a segment, and the physics that it exists. A segment is `machine -> inspector -> findings -> gate -> output`, plus one more arrow Akien drew on 2026-08-14: `-2-> feedback to [thing this thing feeds back to]`. This tool owns that arrow. `route(component)` answers where a component's failing findings go, reading the answer from that component's own charter; `producers()` names every component whose shipped code can construct a finding; `corpus_record()` is the proof record over the pair — one entry per producer, EXPECTED beside ACTUAL, passes included, each passing entry naming the address it proved. `NoRoute` is the refusal, and it is terminal: there is no default destination, because a default is how feedback silently piles up against the wrong door. WHAT `to` MEANS, in his words and not a paraphrase, because the first cast of these routes read the rule as a hop count: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step" (Akien, 2026-08-14). The field names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case and not the definition, so a route out of its own chain — orient's to the ticket — is an ordinary answer rather than a skip that owes anyone an excuse.
why: Akien, 2026-08-14: 'that findings problem IS THIS WHOLE CONVERSATION. That's what we're fixing now. because these have to be as bullet proof as possible. these are the foundation for everything else.' The corpus had been built up to the gate and stopped: MEASURED the day this tool was written, all eight builder stages carried inspector, record, == gate and writer, and edge -2- existed NOWHERE — a grep across the builder, build_inspector and tools/base for any routing declaration returned nothing. Failing findings refused loudly at their gate and stopped travelling, so nothing they could have improved ever heard about them. The lived symptom is Akien's own: a clarifying question at build time meant the chain's intake was short, and the record of it landed in a ledger with no reader and no addressee.
invoke: `from cairn.tools.feedback import feedback` — `feedback.route(component)` for the declared address (raises NoRoute), `feedback.declared(component)` for the raw block, `feedback.producers()` for the population that owes one, `feedback.corpus_record()` for the proof record over the whole corpus. CLI door: `cairn feedbackmap` (bin/cmd/feedbackmap; `--json` for data) — the census of who constructs findings and where each one sends them, exit 0 only when every producer routes. Prove: `python3 cairn/tools/feedback/proofs/test_feedback.py` (exit 0 = green).

feedback.why: A component that ships able to construct findings but unable to route them is a BUILD defect, and build_inspector is the inspector that should have refused it at the crossing — so this tool's own findings go to the inspector that could stop them from ever being emitted again. That is the 'improve the inspector' half of Akien's bound (ruled 2026-08-14) rather than the 'improve the generator' half, and it is the right half here: the generator of a charter is a hand, and a hand is not an address. Deliberately NOT routed to the component each finding names, which was the first instinct: that would be a per-finding destination, and this shape declares one route per segment. If corpus-wide auditors turn out to need per-finding routing, that is a change to the shape and Akien's to make, not a token this tool quietly coins.

node_class: tool — a complete primitive with USERS, not an owner (Law 6). Its users: every component that constructs a finding, and (when it is built) whatever delivers one. STATE: a tool's DEFINITION AND DEFAULTS berth here in class-space; its ONGOING state berths under the holder that assembled it, at `~/.cairn/devices/<device class>/<device name|num>/tools/<tool class>/<tool name|num>/` (ruling 2026-08-14-tools-and-machines-remember-under-their-holder). So a tool can carry class- and instance-level memory — state and history both — with no LLM anywhere near it, 'because each instance of the tool or machine can have it's own data'. And the class segment of that path is a real folder holding all those instances, so it can hold files shared across them — holder-scoped, an affordance of the shape that Akien named explicitly and left unbuilt with no use in mind. That does not dent Law 6: the state hangs off the HOLDER, which is the thing that owns and gates writes to it, so the tool still has nothing OF ITS OWN to gate. The earlier line here read 'a tool holds no state', which states a property of toolhood and is wrong; what is true is narrower and is a fact about this build, not about tools — TODAY this tool persists nothing, reading charters on demand. That changes the moment findings travel (filed edge (a)), and their berth is the address above.
entry: FRESH build, 2026-08-14, out of the conversation that named the gap. Nothing was grafted. Two things were deliberately COMPOSED rather than re-derived: the record shape is `gate.proved` (so a reader who has read one proof record has read this one), and the resolve-or-refuse test for an address is the same move `orient` makes on an invented ref — the thing is on disk or it is not.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter.
how_it_learns: IT DOESN'T, AND ITS WHOLE PURPOSE IS THAT SOMETHING ELSE CAN. This tool is the wire, not the mind on either end of it. What learns is at the far end, and Akien bounded it on 2026-08-14: 'we want to push toward the feedback is processed later to improve the generator and the inspector in most cases' — BOTH ends, the machine that made the bad output and the inspector that missed it or asked the wrong question. That processing act is deliberately not built here and grows against real findings, of which the corpus has none yet. This tool's own contribution to learning is negative and structural: it makes a finding that CANNOT teach anything impossible to have.
gates: This tool's own inspector and gate: `corpus_record()` returns the proof record and `gate.opens()` is the == compare over it, per entry, no oracle. The population it inspects is derived by PARSING (`ast`), never by grepping for `def inspect_` — the rule is about components that can CONSTRUCT a finding, and a name is not a capability. Proof gate: proofs/test_feedback.py (22 teeth). Durability gate: committed + pushed.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) a feedback block with no `why` is accepted — the why is forced by the schema, and a fillable field is the defect this corpus keeps catching; (2) a `to` that does not resolve on disk is stored rather than refused, which would make the field prose again; (3) the population is computed by substring scan, so a module that merely DISCUSSES `proved(` in a docstring is enrolled — use-vs-mention, and this file's own text would trip it; (4) a finding constructed inside `proofs/` makes its component a producer, when a proof is not a segment with an output anyone consumes; (5) a HEALTHY world — every producer routed — yields anything other than an all-passing record and an OPEN gate (the authoring hazard, measured n=4 on 2026-08-13); (6) a component that stops constructing findings turns its entry GREEN instead of removing it, so the record gets cleaner rather than shorter; (7) a route is accepted as a keyword argument at a finding-construction site, which would put the destination at 66 call sites beside a charter that already says it — two mouths on one question, which is the exact defect the proof record was built to close; (8) any default destination is introduced for a component that declares none.
proof: proofs/test_feedback.py — 22 teeth. The load-bearing ones: the WHY is refused when blank or whitespace (schema, not etiquette); an unresolvable `to` refuses; a module that only MENTIONS the constructors inside a string is NOT a producer while one that calls them IS (parsed, not grepped — the tooth a substring build fails on this very proof's docstring); a healthy fixture produces an all-passing record and an OPEN gate (the n=4 authoring hazard, which would otherwise let this ship reddening every component forever and read as strict); an unrouted producer yields EXACTLY ONE failing entry carrying its lack; and a component that stops constructing findings leaves NO entry rather than a green one. The live-corpus teeth assert invariants — the population is non-empty, every producer names a real charter-carrying directory, one entry per producer — and never a count, which would red the day anyone converts a component.
owner: A TOOL HAS USERS, NOT AN OWNER (Law 6). Akien owns the definition — the segment shape and the rule that feedback has a declared destination are his, drawn 2026-08-14. CC writes the code and the proofs.
traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel — a finding that never travels is an answered question thrown away, so the same gap is re-derived every time it recurs)
Law 4 (a rule enforced by physics, not policy — 'feedback should go back to the maker' was prose until a routeless producer could be named by an instrument)
Law 5 (intent, its voyage, and its proofs share an address — the route is declared in the component's own charter, not in a central routing table)
Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces — a finding with nowhere to go is an error collapsed into silence at the one surface that should never collapse it)
Law 9 (red is the default — 17 of 17 producers declare no route today, and this tool's job is to make that measurable rather than assumed)
filed_edges: (a) THE DELIVERY IS NOT BUILT. This tool makes the route declarable, resolvable and enforceable; nothing yet carries a failing finding ALONG the edge to the address it names. That is deliberate — the corpus has zero real findings in flight, and building a deliverer for a population of zero is the manager smell. It grows against the first real one. · *ticket owed*

(b) IMMEDIACY IS LEFT ROOM FOR AND NOT BUILT, on Akien's explicit bound (ruled 2026-08-14): 'we will have cases with more immediacy as well, like don't start a new process if each of these costs 10% of cpu and we're already at 80%. but while we're leaving room for those, we're not building or ticketing those now.' So a route is an address and nothing else — no urgency field, no mode, no enum. Leaving room means the shape does not preclude one; adding a placeholder would be building the thing he said not to build. NOT TICKETED, ON PURPOSE.

(c) CLOSED SAME DAY, 2026-08-14 — kept because the state it records is what the instrument was born measuring. It read: 17 producers, 0 routed at the hour this tool was born; the declarations are a design act per component, 'why THAT address and not another' is what the schema forces, and mass-producing 17 whys would be the fillable-field defect one level up. All 17 are now declared, each from the measured link in its own code — the seven chart legs from the `<stage>_ref` their inspectors actually open (orient alone has none, so it routes above the chain to /intent), tools/base from harbor_master's real import of `emit`, and the auditors from Akien's own example ('a build inspection failure might go back to ticketing'). `./bin/cmd/feedbackmap` exits 0 at 18 of 18. What the declaring MEASURED is now edges (e) and (f): two kinds of finding the one-address shape cannot address honestly.

(d) THE POPULATION IS CODE-SHAPED, NOT SEGMENT-SHAPED. `producers()` finds components whose code constructs a finding; Akien's unit is the SEGMENT, which may group several machines or tools under one inspector and gate. Today those coincide because every finding-producer is its own component. The first segment that spans several components will need this to answer at the segment's address rather than each member's. · *ticket owed*

(e) A SEGMENT'S FINDINGS INDICT BOTH SIDES OF ITS DOOR, AND ONE ADDRESS CANNOT SAY SO. Measured while declaring the 17 routes, 2026-08-14: every chart-chain stage's inspector asks two kinds of question — about the UPSTREAM berth it opened (upstream_berth_is_readable, request_identity_rides_the_chain) and about the stage's OWN authored fields (every_constraint_carries_text_source_kind, the installed judges). Akien's rule sends the first kind upstream; the second kind has no upstream party at all, because its author is the /chart ceiling, a hand. The declared route serves the first honestly and the second not at all, and each stage's charter says which of its checks it is serving rather than pretending the route covers them. Splitting a segment's outbound edge by which side of the door a finding indicts is a change to the SHAPE and Akien's to make. · *ticket owed*

(f) THE UPSTREAM PARTY IS SOMETIMES KNOWN ONLY AT FIRING TIME. learning_block and skill_block both inspect a payload handed in by a caller named in the call, not in the charter — and Akien's design for learning blocks is explicitly to 'send a task or whatever back if the inputs are not sufficient AT ALL STEPS' (Akien, 2026-08-01), which is a caller-returned route. A static declaration cannot spell it, so both declare themselves and say why. Kin to edge (e) and to the per-finding-routing question already reserved to Akien: all three are the same shape question — one address per segment, decided once, when the destination is a function of the firing. · *ticket owed*

(g) THREE ROUTES NAME A STORE WHOSE OWNER IS NOT BUILT. orient, build_inspector and ruling all route to CairnCommons/tickets, and Akien named the owner when he corrected orient's route: "the ticketing machine would be the owner of that. and would get the feedback" (Akien, 2026-08-14). MEASURED the same hour: no such component exists — cairn/machines/ holds build_inspector, diagnostic_inspector, learning_block, ruling and skill_block, and nothing in the corpus casts or gates a ticket. So the address is the ARTIFACT rather than its owner, which is honest today and is not the shape he described: an artifact store cannot receive feedback, it can only hold what someone puts in it. This is the same gap `resolves()` already tolerates by design — it asks whether the destination EXISTS, never whether anything there can act. When the ticketing machine is built, the three routes move to it in one act, and that act is the test of whether this edge was real. · *ticket owed*
provenance: Born 2026-08-14, in the conversation where Akien drew the segment. The design went wrong twice on the way and both corrections are load-bearing. FIRST, CC read the inspector as inspecting its own stage's OUTPUT and proposed a per-row attribution judgement to work out where a finding belonged; Akien corrected the model to the segment unit, and the attribution problem dissolved — the destination is DECLARED, so a finding never needs anyone to work out where it goes. The evidence that CC's version could not have worked is measured and sits in askscan's ledger: all five gaps named `verdict` as the stage that ran last, and not one was verdict's to fix. SECOND, the first cast of this tool made `gate.proved` REQUIRE the route, which would have spelled the destination at 66 finding-construction sites beside a charter that already declared it — two mouths on one question, the identical defect the proof record was built to close for refusal sentences. The charter is the single mouth; a deliverer asks `route()` at delivery time and therefore cannot read a stale copy.
